label: Construct holding click
summary: Runs the click action for constructing a holding, from the county window.
details: Going by its name and its use as an `onclick` in the county window, it starts building a holding when its button is clicked. It returns nothing. The game documents nothing more.

label: Go to faction click
summary: Runs the click action that jumps to a faction, from the county window.
details: Going by its name and its use as an `onclick` in the county window, it takes the player to a faction. It returns nothing. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open siege window
summary: Opens a siege window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it, so nothing shows which siege window or for what. It returns nothing.

label: Pan to county capital
summary: Runs a click action that, going by its name, moves the view to the county capital.
details: Vanilla runs it as an `onclick` in the county window. The input does not say what exactly moves (map camera or something else). It returns nothing.

label: Can be realm capital
summary: Whether the holding is a possible choice for the realm capital.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the county window to decide when a button is visible, alone and combined with `HoldingView.CanSetCountyCapital`. The exact rules are not documented, so this rests on the name.

label: Previous holding
summary: Switches the holding view to the previous holding.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it. It returns nothing.

label: The holding view itself
summary: The holding view object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument, for example `recipient.Self` or `Character.Self`. No line uses it on a holding view, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Set county capital
summary: Runs the click action that makes the holding the capital of its county.
details: Going by its name and its use as an `onclick` in the county window. It returns nothing.

label: Set realm capital
summary: Runs the click action that makes the holding the capital of the realm.
details: Going by its name and its use as an `onclick` in the county window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle find vassal list
summary: Opens or closes the window that lists vassals to find, from the county window.
details: Going by its name and its use as an `onclick` in the county window. It returns nothing.

label: The holy order itself
summary: A way to reach the holy order object itself.
details: No line uses it on a holy order. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way (`PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` is passed to a window function), so this rests on the name only.

label: Can be raised
summary: Whether the holy order can be raised (called up) as an army.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it on a holy order. The same name is used on mercenary companies and military event troops to enable or show buttons, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Capital
summary: The place where the holy order is located.
details: Vanilla writes `HolyOrder.GetCapital.GetName` in the order's location tooltip: 'The order is located in ...'. The result has a name the game can print.

label: Hire cost text
summary: A text describing what hiring the holy order costs the player.
details: Vanilla uses it through `HiredTroopItem.GetHolyOrder.GetCostDescForPlayer` as the hire info line in the hired troops list. No line uses it on a holy order directly, so this rests on that hint and the name.

label: Current soldiers
summary: How many soldiers the holy order has right now.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as '[number] soldiers' in the title and hired troops views, and pairs it with `HolyOrder.GetMaxSoldiers` to fill a progress bar.

label: Divergence
summary: The divergence value of the holy order.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it with a divergence icon in the faith view's holy order details. What divergence is for a holy order is not explained in the input.

label: Faith
summary: The faith the holy order belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads the faith's adjective from it (`HolyOrder.GetFaith.GetAdjective`) and uses it as the data context in the military window.

label: Founder
summary: The founder of the holy order.
details: Vanilla prints its short UI name after 'Patron:' in the holy order tooltip. `HolyOrder.GetPatron` also exists; the input does not say how the two differ.

label: Leased titles
summary: The leased titles of the holy order, as a list.
details: Vanilla counts the list for the '[number] Holdings' text in the faith view and uses it as the list shown in the title window and in tooltips. Which side leases to which is not stated in the input.

label: Maximum soldiers
summary: The most soldiers the holy order can have.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla pairs it with `HolyOrder.GetCurrentSoldiers` to draw a progress bar in the title election window.

label: Name
summary: The name of the holy order, as text.
details: Vanilla writes it in the order's location tooltip: 'The [order] is located in ...'. A sibling `HolyOrder.GetNameNoTooltip` also exists.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the holy order, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as a header, inside a tooltip title and as a label on the map.

label: Number of knights
summary: How many knights the holy order has.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it with a knight icon, followed by the plural word for knights in the order's holder's culture.

label: Leader
summary: The character who leads the holy order.
details: Vanilla labels it 'Leader:' in the holy order tooltip and uses it as the data context for the order's map icon.

label: Patron
summary: The patron of the holy order.
details: Vanilla checks whether it is the local player (`HolyOrder.GetPatron.IsLocalPlayer`) to show things in the military window, and uses it as a data context in the military and title windows.

label: Pledged great holy war
summary: The great holy war the holy order has pledged itself to.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it. See also `HolyOrder.IsPledgedToGreatHolyWar`.

label: Rite
summary: The rite linked to the holy order.
details: Vanilla shows its name in the holy order tooltip ('rite: ...') and passes it on as `HolyOrder.GetRite.Self` to the divergence breakdown in the faith and military windows.

label: Soldiers ratio for bar
summary: The share of soldiers the holy order has, ready for a progress bar.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it. The related functions `HolyOrder.GetCurrentSoldiers` and `HolyOrder.GetMaxSoldiers` exist.

label: Tenet
summary: The tenet linked to the holy order.
details: Vanilla checks `HolyOrder.GetTenet.IsValid` before showing things, in the military and title windows, and uses it as a data context. That check suggests it can be empty.

label: Title
summary: The title that stands for the holy order.
details: Vanilla gets the title's holder from it to name the order's knights in the culture's own word, and uses it as the data context of the order's map icon.

label: Worldliness
summary: The worldliness value of the holy order.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla does not use it, and the input does not say what worldliness measures. See `HolyOrder.GetWorldlinessBreakdown` for its parts.

label: Worldliness breakdown
summary: The list of parts that add up to the holy order's worldliness.
details: The game marks it as a promote function that returns a value breakdown. Vanilla does not use it, so this rests on the name and the return type.

label: Is hired
summary: Whether the holy order is hired by someone.
details: Returns yes or no. No line uses it on a holy order. The same name is used on hired troop items in the military window, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Is hired by the player
summary: Whether the holy order is hired by the local player.
details: No line uses it on a holy order. The same name is used on mercenary companies in the hired troops and military windows, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Is military
summary: Whether the holy order is a military order.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla picks between two texts for the faith view's sub title with it, and shows or hides parts of the military window.

label: Is the player the patron
summary: Whether the local player is the patron of the holy order.
details: No line uses it on a holy order directly. The hired troop window calls it through `HiredTroopItem.GetHolyOrder.IsPlayerPatron` to decide what to show, so this rests on that hint and the name.

label: Is pledged to great holy war
summary: Whether the holy order has pledged itself to a great holy war.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Make script scope
summary: Turns the holy order into a script scope that script values and script texts can use.
details: The game marks it as a promote function that returns a scope. No line uses it on a holy order. Vanilla uses `MakeScope` on other types (for example `GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue(...)`) to call script values from texts, so this rests on that.

label: The holy order itself
summary: The holy order object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument, for example `recipient.Self`. No line uses it on a holy order, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: The icon itself
summary: A way to reach the holy order coat of arms icon object itself.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only. The type is the holy order's icon on the map.

label: Holy order
summary: The holy order that the map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the map icon layer, so the icon's parts can read the order's data.

label: Leased province
summary: The leased province that the holy order map icon is about.
details: Vanilla reads its name without tier and tooltip (`GetNameNoTierNoTooltip`) as the label text of the map icon.

label: Is a leased province
summary: Whether the map icon is for a leased-out province.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to switch between two looks of the map icon. The exact meaning of leased out is not given, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: The icon itself
summary: The holy order map icon object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument. No line uses it on this type, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: The holy site itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site object itself.
details: No line uses it on a holy site. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Active effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site does while it is active.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla uses it in the faith window's holy site tooltip. The input does not show the argument; the sibling `HolySite.GetInactiveEffectDesc` is called with a faith in the game's GUI, so a faith is a likely but unconfirmed guess.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the input does not name it.

label: Barony
summary: The barony where the holy site is.
details: Vanilla reads the barony's province and its holding from it, and passes it on (`HolySite.GetBarony.Self`) to effect descriptions of the site's type.

label: Controller
summary: The one who controls the holy site.
details: Vanilla reads `HolySite.GetController.GetRite` in the faith window, so the result is something that has a rite. The input does not say what kind of object it is.

label: County
summary: The county where the holy site is.
details: Vanilla asks it for its holder (`.GetHolder`) and whether it has one (`.HasHolder`) in the faith and holy site windows.

label: Effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site does, for a given argument.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla uses it in the artifact ledger's holy site tooltip. What the argument is is not shown in the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the input does not name it.

label: Faiths
summary: The faiths linked to the holy site.
details: No line uses it on a holy site. The same name is used on the religion and rite windows to list faiths, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Inactive effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site would do while it is inactive, for a given faith.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla uses it in the faith window tooltip and in the holy site window as `HolySite.GetInactiveEffectDesc( Faith.Self )`, so the argument is a faith.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The faith to describe the effect for.

label: Inventory
summary: The inventory of the holy site, where artifacts are kept.
details: Vanilla reads its artifacts with `HolySite.GetInventory.GetArtifacts` for the faith window's list.

label: Inventory text
summary: A text describing what the holy site's inventory gives, for a given argument.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla uses it in the holy site tooltips of the decisions and the faith window. What the argument is is not shown in the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the input does not name it.

label: Name
summary: The name of the holy site, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as 'The site becomes an eminent holy site of the faith'. A sibling `HolySite.GetNameNoTooltip` also exists.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the holy site, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in tooltip titles and in the faith view's site list, and compares it with the type's name to choose the window header.

label: Related building type
summary: The building type that belongs to the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the holy site window. Which building is meant is not given in the input.

label: Active artifact rarity total
summary: The sum of the rarity of the artifacts that are active at the holy site.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla draws a progress bar of it against the game define `MAX_HOLY_SITE_RARITY_TOTAL` in the holy site window.

label: Type
summary: The holy site type of the holy site.
details: Vanilla reads the type's name and its effect text from it, and compares the name with the site's own name to choose the window header.

label: Is active
summary: Whether the holy site is active.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to show different parts of the holy site window and the faith window.

label: Is holy site type
summary: Whether the holy site is of a given type.
details: It takes one argument and returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it, so the argument is not shown; going by the name it is a holy site type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the input does not name it.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the holy site exists, that is, whether there is a holy site to read from.
details: Returns yes or no. No line uses it on a holy site; `IsValid` is used in the same way on many other types, where it guards against an empty value.

label: Make script scope
summary: Turns the holy site into a script scope that a decision can use.
details: Vanilla passes it as the 'selected_item' parameter when it builds the elevate, demote and abandon holy site decisions in the holy site window (`MakeDecisionTypeWithParam`).

label: The holy site itself
summary: The holy site object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example `Faith.IsEminentHolySite( HolySite.Self )` asks whether a faith treats this site as eminent.

label: Cost breakdown
summary: The breakdown of what creating the holy site costs, as a data context.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the holy site creation window. The input says no more, so the breakdown idea rests on the name.

label: The window itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site creation window object itself.
details: No line uses it on this window. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can create
summary: Whether the holy site can be created from the window.
details: Returns yes or no. No line uses it on this window. The artifact helper window has a function of the same name that enables a button, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Can pick holy site type
summary: Whether the given holy site type can be chosen in the window.
details: It takes one holy site type and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the type's button: `CanPickHolySiteType( HolySiteType.Self )`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The holy site type to check.

label: Can remove enshrined artifact
summary: Whether the given enshrined artifact can be removed from the holy site.
details: It takes one artifact and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable a remove button: `CanRemoveEnshrinedArtifact( Artifact.Self )`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to check.

label: Clear selected artifact
summary: Clears the artifact that is selected in the window.
details: Returns nothing. No line uses it on this window. The royal court window has a function of the same name that runs on click, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Close
summary: Closes the holy site creation window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of a button in the window.

label: Faiths with an active site
summary: The list of faiths for which a holy site is active.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list shown in the window and hides the list when it is empty. Going by the name, these are the faiths the site is active for.

label: Available holy site types
summary: The list of holy site types that can be chosen in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the window and shows a notice when the list is empty.

label: Cost description
summary: A text describing what creating the holy site costs.
details: Vanilla puts it after 'Cost:' in the window's action cost line.

label: Create button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the create button.
details: Vanilla uses it at the start of the tooltip shown when the create button is disabled, followed by extra lines.

label: Creation blockers
summary: A text listing what prevents the holy site from being created.
details: No line uses it on this window. The rite creation window has a function of the same name used in its create and reform tooltips, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Enshrinable artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts that can be enshrined in the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list of artifacts in the window and shows a notice when the list is empty.

label: Enshrine tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for enshrining the given artifact.
details: It takes one artifact. Vanilla writes it as `GetEnshrineTooltip( Artifact.Self )` for the artifact's entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact the tooltip is about.

label: Faith
summary: The faith the holy site creation window is about.
details: Vanilla uses its icon, passes it on as `.Self` to the holy site type's effect texts, and uses it as the data context in the window.

label: Chosen holy site type
summary: The holy site type picked in the window.
details: Vanilla checks `IsValid` on it to see whether a type is picked, and uses it as the data context of the window's parts.

label: Holy site type tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the given holy site type.
details: It takes one holy site type. Vanilla writes it as `GetHolySiteTypeTooltip( HolySiteType.Self )` in the tooltip of a type button, after the type's name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The holy site type the tooltip is about.

label: Faiths with an inactive site
summary: The list of faiths for which a holy site is inactive.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list shown in the window and hides the list when it is empty. Going by the name, these are the faiths the site is not active for.

label: Possible baronies
summary: The list of barony titles that can be chosen for the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list of baronies the player can pick in the window.

label: Remove button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the remove button.
details: No line uses it on this window. The holy site window uses a function of the same name for a tooltip, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Remove tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for removing the given artifact.
details: It takes one artifact. Vanilla writes it as `GetRemoveTooltip( Artifact.Self )` for a text and for a tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact the tooltip is about.

label: Selected action effect text
summary: A text describing what the selected action does.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window. What the action is, exactly, is not given in the input.

label: Selected artifact
summary: The artifact picked in the window.
details: Vanilla checks `IsValid` on it, together with the chosen type, to decide what to show. So it can be empty.

label: Selected artifacts
summary: The artifacts picked in the window, as a list.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it in this form. A similar call, `GetSelectedArtifactsRaritySum`, is used.

label: Selected artifacts rarity sum
summary: The sum of the rarity of the artifacts picked in the window.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it as text and, as a whole number, in a progress bar against the define `MAX_HOLY_SITE_RARITY_TOTAL`.

label: Selected barony
summary: The barony picked in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, reads its holding's name, and passes it on as `.Self` to the type's name and effect texts.

label: Slots
summary: The list of slots shown in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the window. What the slots hold is not given in the input; going by the window, probably artifact slots.

label: Has selected artifact
summary: Whether an artifact is picked in the window.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the choice of values passed to the type's regular and eminent effect texts.

label: Has selected barony
summary: Whether a barony is picked in the window.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it, and its opposite, to show different parts of the window.

label: Is artifact selected
summary: Whether the given artifact is the one picked in the window.
details: It takes one artifact and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of an artifact's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to check.

label: Is barony selected
summary: Whether the given barony is the one picked in the window.
details: It takes one barony title and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a barony's button and to show a mark.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The barony to check.

label: Is create button enabled
summary: Whether the create button can be clicked.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the button and to choose between two tooltip texts.

label: Is holy site type selected
summary: Whether the given holy site type is the one picked in the window.
details: It takes one holy site type and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a type's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The holy site type to check.

label: Is remove button enabled
summary: Whether the remove button can be clicked.
details: Returns yes or no. No line uses it on this window. The holy site window uses a function of the same name to enable a button, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Is selecting barony
summary: Whether the window is in the mode where a barony is being picked.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show a hint and as the pressed state of the pick button. See `StartSelectBarony` and `StopSelectBarony`, which switch the mode.

label: On create
summary: Runs the creation of the holy site.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it. The button itself uses `OnCreateButtonClicked`.

label: Create button click
summary: Runs the click action of the create button.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of the create button.

label: Remove button click
summary: Runs the click action of the remove button.
details: Returns nothing. No line uses it on this window; the holy site window uses a function of the same name as an `onclick`, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Select artifact
summary: Picks the given artifact in the window.
details: It takes one artifact and returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of an artifact's entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to pick.

label: Select barony
summary: Picks the given barony in the window.
details: It takes one barony title and returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of a barony entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The barony to pick.

label: Select holy site type
summary: Picks the given holy site type in the window.
details: It takes one holy site type and returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of a type's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The holy site type to pick.

label: The window itself
summary: The holy site creation window object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument. No line uses it on this window, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Start selecting barony
summary: Switches the window into the mode where a barony is picked.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of a button. See `IsSelectingBarony` for the matching check.

label: Stop selecting barony
summary: Switches the window out of the mode where a barony is picked.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of a button.

label: The icon itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site map icon object itself.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Holy site item
summary: The holy site item that the map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the map icon layer, so the icon's parts can read the item's data.

label: The icon itself
summary: The holy site map icon object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument. No line uses it on this type, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: The item itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site item object itself.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Control text
summary: A text describing who controls the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the holy site window and in the faith window's holy site tooltip.

label: Faith
summary: The faith that the holy site item belongs to.
details: Vanilla asks it whether a site is eminent for it (`Faith.IsEminentHolySite`) and passes it on as `.Self` to the type's effect texts.

label: Holy site
summary: The holy site of the item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context on the map and asks it whether it is active (`GetHolySite.IsActive`).

label: Is eminent
summary: Whether the holy site is an eminent holy site for the item's faith.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla combines it with whether the site is held and active to decide which marks show in the faith window.

label: Is held by the faith
summary: Whether the faith itself holds the holy site.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to colour the site's name, to pick tooltip text and to show different marks in the faith window and on the map.

label: The item itself
summary: The holy site item object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses `.Self` on many types to hand an object to a function that wants it as an argument. No line uses it on this type, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: The type itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site type object itself.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Custom text
summary: Calls a custom localization text with the holy site type.
details: It takes one argument, the key of the custom text. Vanilla uses `.Custom( 'key' )` on other types such as characters; no line uses it on a holy site type, so this rests on that.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization to call.
fields.values: a quoted text key, for example `'MyCustomText'`

label: All effects text
summary: A text describing all effects of the holy site type.
details: It takes three arguments, which the input does not name. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: Third argument; the input does not name it.

label: Barony
summary: A barony tied to the holy site type, going by its name.
details: No line uses it on a holy site type. The same name is used on holding items and on holy sites to read a barony, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the holy site type.
details: No line uses it on a holy site type. The same name is used for descriptions of buildings and government types, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Dynamic name
summary: The name of the holy site type, worked out for a given barony.
details: It takes one barony. Vanilla writes it as `GetDynamicName( HolySiteCreationWindow.GetSelectedBarony.Self )`, so the name may depend on the barony.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The barony the name is made for.

label: Effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site type does for a faith at a barony.
details: It takes two arguments. Vanilla writes it as `GetEffectDesc( HolySiteItem.GetFaith.Self, HolySite.GetBarony.Self )`: the faith first, then the barony.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The faith the effect is described for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The barony of the site.

label: Eminent effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site type does when the site is eminent.
details: It takes three arguments. Vanilla writes the window's faith first, then the selected barony, then `Select_CFixedPoint( HasSelectedArtifact, GetSelectedArtifactsRaritySum, -1 )`: the rarity sum of the picked artifacts when one is picked, otherwise -1. What the function does with that number is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The faith the effect is described for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The barony of the site.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A number; vanilla passes the rarity sum of the picked artifacts, or -1 when none is picked.

label: Eminent scaled effect text
summary: A text describing the eminent effect of the holy site type, scaled by a value.
details: It takes three arguments, which the input does not name. Vanilla does not use it; the name suggests a scaled variant of `GetEminentEffectDesc`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: Third argument; the input does not name it.

label: Log name
summary: The name of the holy site type as used in logs.
details: Going by its name only; vanilla does not use it.

label: Name
summary: The name of the holy site type, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the type's tooltip titles and in the warning that a faith already has a holy site of this type.

label: Regular effect text
summary: A text describing what the holy site type does when the site is regular (not eminent).
details: It takes three arguments. Vanilla writes the window's faith first, then the selected barony, then `Select_CFixedPoint( HasSelectedArtifact, GetSelectedArtifactsRaritySum, -1 )`: the rarity sum of the picked artifacts when one is picked, otherwise -1. What the function does with that number is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The faith the effect is described for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The barony of the site.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A number; vanilla passes the rarity sum of the picked artifacts, or -1 when none is picked.

label: Regular scaled effect text
summary: A text describing the regular effect of the holy site type, scaled by a value.
details: It takes three arguments, which the input does not name. Vanilla does not use it; the name suggests a scaled variant of `GetRegularEffectDesc`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: Third argument; the input does not name it.

label: Static effect text
summary: A text describing the fixed effects of the holy site type.
details: It takes two arguments, which the input does not name. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the input does not name it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the input does not name it.

label: Has parameter
summary: Whether the holy site type has the given parameter.
details: It takes one argument and returns yes or no. No line uses it on a holy site type; the same name is used on other types, such as situation phase types, with a parameter name. This rests on that.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the parameter to look for.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether a holy site type is set.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the creation window to show different parts depending on whether a type is picked.

label: Make script scope
summary: Turns the holy site type into a script scope that script values and script texts can use.
details: The game marks it as a promote function that returns a scope. No line uses it on a holy site type. Vanilla uses `MakeScope` on other types (for example `GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue(...)`), so this rests on that.

label: The type itself
summary: The holy site type object itself, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument in the creation window, for example `CanPickHolySiteType( HolySiteType.Self )` and `SelectHolySiteType( HolySiteType.Self )`.

label: The window itself
summary: A way to reach the holy site window object itself.
details: No line uses it on this window. Other types use `AccessSelf` in the same way, so this rests on the name only.

label: Can enshrine artifact
summary: Whether the given artifact can be enshrined in the holy site.
details: It takes one argument and returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it, so this rests on the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to check; the input does not name it.

label: Can remove enshrined artifact
summary: Whether the given enshrined artifact can be removed from the holy site.
details: It takes one artifact and returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable a remove button: `CanRemoveEnshrinedArtifact( Artifact.Self )`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to check.

label: Clear selected slot
summary: Clears the slot that is selected in the window.
details: Returns nothing. No line uses it on this window. The inventory window has a function of the same name that runs on click, so this rests on the name and that hint.

label: Close
summary: Closes the holy site window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it as the `onclick` of several buttons in the window.

label: Equip artifact
summary: Equips the given artifact, going by its name.
details: It takes one argument and returns nothing. Vanilla does not use it, so this rests on the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact to equip; the input does not name it.

label: Faiths with an active site
summary: The list of faiths for which the holy site is active.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list in the window, shows its size in the header 'Holy Site for faiths (number)' and hides the list when it is empty.

label: Artifact sort options
summary: The list of ways to sort artifacts in the window.
details: No line uses it on this window. The inventory and royal court windows use a function of the same name as a list, so this rests on the name and those uses.

label: Faith to compare to
summary: The faith the window compares the holy site against.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and compares it with another faith (`ObjectsEqual( Faith.Self, ... )`) to decide what to show.

label: Enshrinable artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts that can be enshrined in the holy site.
details: Vanilla uses it as the artifact list and shows its size as a number.

label: Enshrine button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the enshrine button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of two buttons in the window.

label: Enshrine tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for enshrining the given artifact.
details: It takes one artifact. Vanilla writes it as `GetEnshrineTooltip( Artifact.Self )` for the artifact's entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact the tooltip is about.

label: Holy site
summary: The holy site that the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window, and reads its inventory from it.

label: Holy site item
summary: The holy site item that the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the window.
